title: SLO delegation and eviction credit accounting for pinned model variants
creator: Emily Zhao
description:
Problem: Customers pin model variants to guarantee quality (e.g., full precision or specific finetuned weights). During regional capacity pressure or degraded hardware, pinned variants cannot be evicted automatically without violating customer expectations. Current global SLO accounting treats pinned variants the same as unpinned ones which leads to unfair error-budget burns and opaque throttles.

Goal: Define an operational policy and SLO manifest that: (1) delegates a portion of tenant error budget to pinned variants via an 'eviction credit' accounting model; (2) prescribes when and how to forcibly degrade or gently redirect pinned traffic across regions; (3) ensures transparent billing/alerting and predictable failover for customers with pinned variants.

Scope: per-endpoint per-variant SLI/SLO definitions, credit accrual/consumption algorithms, ownership and alerting semantics, dashboards and runtime enforcement hooks. Works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Non-goals: Replacing the overall endpoint SLO framework or changing global error-budget math for unpinned variants. This ticket focuses on delegation and accounting semantics only.
acceptance_criteria: Formal SLO manifest fields documented for pinned variants (manifest schema and examples).
Eviction credit accrual formula and charge rules validated against historical traffic (sample runbook attached).
Runtime enforcement RFC with circuit-breaker thresholds and multi-region reroute decision tree reviewed by SRE and Product.
Alerting rules and dashboard tiles added to per-tenant console explaining remaining eviction credits and projected depletion time.
Integration tests exercising credit depletion -> gentle degrade -> forced fallback path implemented in a staging cluster.
Customer-facing docs draft explaining implications and upgrade path for pinned variant customers.
Proposal reviewed and acknowledged by legal/compliance for contracts that reference pinned variants.
notes: Design trade-off: conservative credits preserve customer expectations but increase blast radius on capacity-constrained regions. We recommend tiered credits (enterprise vs standard).
Credit model chosen: time-weighted token credits + burst reserve. See formula in Confluence link.
We evaluated two approaches for eviction triggers: simple threshold (percent of regional capacity) vs burn-rate-based trigger (uses projected depletion). Burn-rate chosen for smoother behavior.
Edge-case: pinned variants with GPU affinity (specific hardware) will be exempt from cross-region reroute unless customer opts-in. This requires contract flag and will appear in Console UI.

Billing implication: when pinned variant is forcibly routed to a higher-cost region, customer is notified and given 48h window to opt-out; after that default billing policy applies. Finance review pending.

Product: require explicit customer acknowledgement before billing changes when fallback costs increase (accepted).

Research/ML: ensure quality regression metrics are captured when variant fallback occurs (requested: add new SLI 'quality-delta').
